overall_summary: Space-themed content focusing on extreme cosmic anomalies, sensory paradoxes, and mind-bending comparisons significantly outperforms abstract psychology and repetitive animal facts. Shorter, punchier durations of 15-16 seconds yield the highest engagement and views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Paradoxes & Sensory Space Facts
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' achieved 1,053 views, 'The Largest Ocean in Space' reached 460 views, and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' hit 368 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space anomalies that challenge basic physics or human senses, utilizing high-contrast visual hooks in the first 3 seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' generated 302 views, showing strong curiosity-driven CTR.
winning_patterns.action: Create content comparing historical timelines or biological facts that sound impossible but are scientifically true.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (max 52 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently underperformed.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from generic psychological advice or internal brain functions unless they can be framed with a highly dramatic, externalized visual hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 vs 183 views) and 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 vs 52 views) show highly volatile and generally low baseline performance.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid re-uploading identical concepts; instead, iterate on successful angles by changing the core subject or introducing a new twist.

next_video.concept: TrES-2b, the pitch-black planet that glows like a burning ember.
next_video.opening_direction: Show a pitch-black screen with the hook: 'This planet is blacker than coal, absorbing 99% of all light...'
next_video.twist_direction: ...but it's actually a burning hellscape, glowing with a ghostly, silent red light.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven success of extreme planetary anomalies (like the 1,053-view 'Burning Ice' video) using a high-contrast visual paradox that fits the optimal 15-second retention sweet spot.

experiment: Test a 15-second 'Impossible History' Short comparing the age of two highly recognizable historical elements (e.g., Cleopatra lived closer to the iPhone than the building of the Great Pyramid) to see if chronological juxtaposition can replicate the success of the 'Sharks vs. Trees' video.
